audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for wedding feast parable, garment warning, Caesar tax question, Sadducees/resurrection, greatest command, and Messiah/Son of David question.

verses.restored: Jesus answered again in parables, saying to them:

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and spake unto them again by parables, and said,

modern.text: Once again, Jesus spoke to them in parables:

original.text: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν εἶπεν ⸂ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς⸃ λέγων·

verses.restored: The reign of the heavens is like a human king who made a wedding feast for his son.

familiar.text: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son,

modern.text: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.

original.text: Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ, ὅστις ἐποίησεν γάμους τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding feast, but they were not willing to come.

familiar.text: And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come.

modern.text: He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come.

original.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ καλέσαι τοὺς κεκλημένους εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελον ἐλθεῖν.

verses.restored: Again he sent other servants, saying, Tell those invited: Look, my meal is prepared; my oxen and fattened animals are sacrificed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.

familiar.text: Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage.

modern.text: Again, he sent other servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’

original.text: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους λέγων· Εἴπατε τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἰδοὺ τὸ ἄριστόν μου ⸀ἡτοίμακα, οἱ ταῦροί μου καὶ τὰ σιτιστὰ τεθυμένα, καὶ πάντα ἕτοιμα· δεῦτε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.

verses.restored: But they paid no attention and went away, one to his own field, another to his trade.

familiar.text: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise:

modern.text: But they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπῆλθον, ⸀ὃς μὲν εἰς τὸν ἴδιον ἀγρόν, ⸁ὃς δὲ ⸀ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμπορίαν αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.

familiar.text: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them.

modern.text: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.

original.text: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ κρατήσαντες τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὕβρισαν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.

verses.restored: The king was enraged; he sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.

familiar.text: But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.

modern.text: The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.

original.text: ⸂ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς⸃ ὠργίσθη, καὶ πέμψας τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν τοὺς φονεῖς ἐκείνους καὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτῶν ἐνέπρησεν.

verses.restored: Then he said to his servants, The wedding feast is ready, but those invited were not worthy.

familiar.text: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy.

modern.text: Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy.

original.text: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι·

verses.restored: Therefore go to the crossroads of the ways, and invite to the wedding feast as many as you find.

familiar.text: Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.

modern.text: Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.’

original.text: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν, καὶ ὅσους ⸀ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους.

verses.restored: Those servants went out into the ways and gathered all whom they found, both harmful and good; and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

familiar.text: So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.

modern.text: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας ⸀οὓς εὗρον, πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς· καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ ⸀γάμος ἀνακειμένων.

verses.restored: When the king entered to behold the guests, he saw there a person not wearing a wedding garment.

familiar.text: And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:

modern.text: But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.

original.text: εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου·

verses.restored: He said to him, Friend, how did you enter here without a wedding garment? But he was speechless.

familiar.text: And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.

modern.text: ‘Friend,’ he asked, ‘how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But the man was speechless.

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου; ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη.

verses.restored: Then the king said to the servants, Bind his feet and hands and cast him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.

familiar.text: Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

modern.text: Then the king told the servants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

original.text: τότε ⸂ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν⸃ τοῖς διακόνοις· Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ⸂ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν⸃ εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.

verses.restored: For many are called, but few are chosen.

familiar.text: For many are called, but few are chosen.

modern.text: For many are called, but few are chosen.” Paying Taxes to Caesar (Mark 12:13–17; Luke 20:19–26)

original.text: πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί.

verses.restored: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might trap him in word.

familiar.text: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk.

modern.text: Then the Pharisees went out and conspired to trap Jesus in His words.

original.text: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ.

verses.restored: They sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know you are true and teach the way of the Divine in truth, and you do not care about anyone's status, for you do not look at people's face.

familiar.text: And they sent out unto him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Master, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man: for thou regardest not the person of men.

modern.text: They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance.

original.text: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ⸀λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις, καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων·

verses.restored: Tell us, then, what do you think? Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

familiar.text: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?

modern.text: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”

original.text: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν τί σοι δοκεῖ· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ;

verses.restored: Knowing their harmful intent, Jesus said, Why do you test me, hypocrites?

familiar.text: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?

modern.text: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?

original.text: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Τί με πειράζετε, ὑποκριταί;

verses.restored: Show me the coin of the tribute. They brought him a denarius.

familiar.text: Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny.

modern.text: Show Me the coin used for the tax.” And they brought Him a denarius.

original.text: ἐπιδείξατέ μοι τὸ νόμισμα τοῦ κήνσου. οἱ δὲ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δηνάριον.

verses.restored: He said to them, Whose image and inscription is this?

familiar.text: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?

modern.text: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή;

verses.restored: They said, Caesar's. Then he said to them, Give back, therefore, the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of the Divine to the Divine.

familiar.text: They say unto him, Caesar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

modern.text: “Caesar’s,” they answered. So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

original.text: λέγουσιν ⸀αὐτῷ· Καίσαρος. τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: Hearing this, they marveled; leaving him, they went away.

familiar.text: When they had heard these words, they marvelled, and left him, and went their way.

modern.text: And when they heard this, they were amazed. So they left Him and went away. The Sadducees and the Resurrection (Mark 12:18–27; Luke 20:27–40)

original.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν, καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν.

verses.restored: On that day Sadducees came to him, those saying there is no resurrection, and they questioned him,

familiar.text: The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,

modern.text: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him.

original.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι, ⸀λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν, καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν

verses.restored: saying, Teacher, Moses said, If someone dies having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up seed for his brother.

familiar.text: Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

modern.text: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.

original.text: λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα, ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: There were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no seed, left his wife to his brother.

familiar.text: Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased, and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother:

modern.text: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died without having children. So he left his wife to his brother.

original.text: ἦσαν δὲ παρʼ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ⸀γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν, καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: Likewise the second and third, down to the seventh.

familiar.text: Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.

modern.text: The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh.

original.text: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος, ἕως τῶν ἑπτά·

verses.restored: Last of all, the woman died.

familiar.text: And last of all the woman died also.

modern.text: And last of all, the woman died.

original.text: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ⸀ἡ γυνή.

verses.restored: In the resurrection, then, of which of the seven will she be wife? For they all had her.

familiar.text: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.

modern.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.”

original.text: ἐν τῇ ⸂ἀναστάσει οὖν⸃ τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή; πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν.

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, You are wandering, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of the Divine.

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.

original.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ·

verses.restored: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like messengers in heaven.

familiar.text: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.

modern.text: In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

original.text: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε ⸀γαμίζονται, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἄγγελοι ⸀θεοῦ ἐν ⸀τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν·

verses.restored: Concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by the Divine, saying,

familiar.text: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,

modern.text: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:

original.text: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ λέγοντος·

verses.restored: I am the Divine of Abraham, the Divine of Isaac, and the Divine of Jacob? He is not Divine of dead ones, but of living ones.

familiar.text: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.

modern.text: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ ? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”

original.text: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ; οὐκ ἔστιν ⸂ὁ θεὸς⸃ νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων.

verses.restored: When the crowds heard, they were astonished at his teaching.

familiar.text: And when the multitude heard this, they were astonished at his doctrine.

modern.text: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching. The Greatest Commandment (Deuteronomy 6:1–19; Mark 12:28–34)

original.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: When the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.

familiar.text: But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.

modern.text: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.

original.text: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.

verses.restored: One of them, a legal expert, asked, testing him:

familiar.text: Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him, and saying,

modern.text: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:

original.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων ⸀αὐτόν·

verses.restored: Teacher, which command is great in the Law?

familiar.text: Master, which is the great commandment in the law?

modern.text: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”

original.text: Διδάσκαλε, ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ;

verses.restored: He said to him, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul/life, and with all your mind.

familiar.text: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.

modern.text: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’

original.text: ὁ ⸀δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ ⸀τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ ⸁τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου·

verses.restored: This is the great and first command.

familiar.text: This is the first and great commandment.

modern.text: This is the first and greatest commandment.

original.text: αὕτη ἐστὶν ⸂ἡ μεγάλη καὶ πρώτη⸃ ἐντολή.

verses.restored: A second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

familiar.text: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

modern.text: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’

original.text: Δευτέρα ⸀δὲ ὁμοία ⸀αὐτῇ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

verses.restored: On these two commands hang all the Law and the Prophets.

familiar.text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

modern.text: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.” Whose Son Is the Christ? (Mark 12:35–37; Luke 20:41–44)

original.text: ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος ⸂κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται⸃.

verses.restored: While the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus questioned them,

familiar.text: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them,

modern.text: While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus questioned them:

original.text: Συνηγμένων δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς

verses.restored: saying, What do you think about the Messiah? Whose son is he? They said to him, David's.

familiar.text: Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The son of David.

modern.text: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” “David’s,” they answered.

original.text: λέγων· Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ περὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ; τίνος υἱός ἐστιν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Τοῦ Δαυίδ.

verses.restored: He said to them, How then does David in Spirit call him Lord, saying,

familiar.text: He saith unto them, How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying,

modern.text: Jesus said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’? For he says:

original.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Πῶς οὖν Δαυὶδ ἐν πνεύματι ⸂καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον⸃ λέγων·

verses.restored: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet?

familiar.text: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool?

modern.text: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

original.text: ⸀Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ⸀ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου;

verses.restored: If David calls him Lord, how is he his son?

familiar.text: If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?

modern.text: So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?”

original.text: εἰ οὖν Δαυὶδ καλεῖ αὐτὸν κύριον, πῶς υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν;

verses.restored: No one was able to answer him a word, nor from that day did anyone dare to question him further.

familiar.text: And no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.

modern.text: No one was able to answer a word, and from that day on no one dared to question Him any further.

original.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ⸂ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ⸃ λόγον, οὐδὲ ἐτόλμησέν τις ἀπʼ ἐκείνης τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐκέτι.
